outcome: number of bolus doses of vasopressors required
cohort: 126 women aged 22-40 years with singleton pregnancy classified to the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical class I and II posted for elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia
finding: Intermittent boluses of norepinephrine are found to be more effective in the management of spinal-induced hypotension during caesarean section compared to phenylephrine.
